why:
Checks 1 and 2 pass; check 3 fails on two independent grounds, so the row is refuted as a divergence.

(1) QUOTE VERBATIM: confirmed. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/accessibility.md line 115 is exactly `* The \`theme\` [setting](/docs/en/settings#available-settings) selects the interface colors, including the colorblind-friendly \`dark-daltonized\` and \`light-daltonized\` themes.` It is a single-sentence bullet in the '## Accessibility settings beyond screen reader mode' list; no second clause reverses it.

(2) CITED FILE:LINE: confirmed exactly. packages/shared/src/config/theme.ts:49 is `export type ThemeMode = 'solid' | 'scenic';` and :55 is `export interface ThemeOverrides extends ThemeColors, SurfaceColors {` with `dark?: ThemeColors & SurfaceColors;` at :57. `grep -rani` (case-insensitive, -a so NUL-byte files are not skipped) for daltonized/colorblind/color-blind/deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia over packages+apps returns 0 product hits -- the only hits are the doc-sweep's own JSON/markdown rows.

(3a) DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE, RECORDED IN SHIPPED CODE. Claude's `theme` is a TERMINAL palette for a TUI: settings.md:333 lists the enum as auto/dark/light/dark-daltonized/light-daltonized/dark-ansi/light-ansi and links to terminal-config#create-a-custom-theme -- the daltonized variants sit in the same enum as the `-ansi` ones. Nessy Desktop is an Electron GUI, and the fork has an explicit, reasoned refusal of that whole vocabulary at packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2219-2251: 'REFUSED, deliberately, rather than loaded... Nessy's theming is a web token set (config/theme.ts ...) and `base` has no counterpart at all... Nothing in the format defines a mapping between the two vocabularies, so loading one would mean inventing it', with an author-facing diagnostic `plugin.format.claude_theme_unsupported`. The `base` presets that decision refuses are precisely dark/light/dark-daltonized/light-daltonized/dark-ansi/light-ansi. So the absence of a `dark-daltonized` theme is the documented consequence of a recorded decision about a TUI-vs-GUI vocabulary mismatch, not an unnoticed gap. (It is not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 -- the decision lives in the adapter source instead.)

(3b) THE CLAIMED OUR-STATE MISCHARACTERISES THE FORK'S THEME MODEL, and the cited evidence does not support it. theme.ts:49/:55 are the *override* type, not the theme-selection surface. The fork does have a named-theme selection surface -- the actual counterpart to Claude's `theme` setting: six bundled presets (Codex, GitHub, Haze, Nord, One Dark Pro, Vitesse) at apps/electron/resources/themes/*.json, seeded into ~/.nessy-agent/themes/ by ensurePresetThemes (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:1909-1955), hot-reloaded by the config watcher (packages/shared/src/config/watcher.ts:1125-1144), and selected over RPC via theme:getPresets / theme:loadPreset (packages/shared/src/protocol/channels.ts:131-132). Each theme file carries the six semantic colours plus five surface colours as arbitrary CSS colours (themeToCSS, theme.ts:178-225), so a colour-vision-adjusted palette is authorable today as a JSON drop-in. 'Our theme model is light/dark colour overrides plus a solid/scenic mode' describes one struct in that system and omits the selection surface entirely.

Residual truth, much narrower than filed: no daltonized palette ships among the six bundled presets. That is a product content wish (add one JSON file), not a divergence from a Claude Code contract our GUI is bound to.
